hypothesis: Price-derived signals collapsed to 2.9 effective independent strategies because they all transform one series. Earnings surprise is generated by a different process (analyst forecast error) and should be weakly correlated with momentum. Post-earnings announcement drift (Ball-Brown 1968, Bernard-Thomas 1989) is among the most replicated anomalies. Predicting: standalone IC of 0.01-0.03, and more importantly correlation below 0.1 with the existing price book, which would raise effective breadth above 2.9 and is the thing that actually matters for the Sharpe target.

hypothesis: The signal is held fixed; only the map from signal to positions changes. Equal-weighted quintile sorts discard the middle 60% of the cross-section and give every name in a bucket identical weight regardless of conviction or risk. Four standard constructions taken from practice, declared before testing: (a) equal-weight quintile baseline, (b) signal-weighted across the full cross-section, (c) risk-adjusted signal weighting z/sigma, (d) factor-neutralized residual then risk-weighted. Prediction: (c) and (d) beat (a) because removing uncompensated variance raises the ratio without needing a better signal. Target is SPY at 0.91 from a current 0.65.
name: portfolio construction: risk weighting and factor neutralization

note: CRITICAL: portfolio construction did not help (quintile 0.39 beat signal-weighted 0.09, risk-adj 0.02, factor-neutral -0.16) and cost drag was flat at ~0.48% across all four, so costs were not the explanation. factor attribution shows the earnings signal IS beta+momentum: score correlates +0.104 with 126d momentum, and residualizing against beta/size/momentum takes the large-cap book from 0.34 to -0.17. no independent alpha

hypothesis: Every signal tested so far is a function of past prices, which is why the best book residualized to -0.17 against beta, size and momentum. Insider transactions and short interest are generated by human decisions rather than price history. Literature: Lakonishok-Lee 2001 and Jeng-Metrick-Zeckhauser 2003 find insider PURCHASES predict positive returns while sales are mostly uninformative (diversification); Boehmer-Jones-Zhang find heavily shorted stocks underperform. The test that matters is not the raw Sharpe but whether the return SURVIVES factor neutralization, which nothing has so far.
name: insider buying (SEC Form 4) and short interest

note: FIRST SIGNAL TO SURVIVE FACTOR NEUTRALIZATION. short_ratio residual sharpe 1.66 t=3.90 (raw was 0.51); days_to_cover near-identical (same underlying measure). survives every robustness check: excluding 2021 meme era gives 1.69, from mid-2022 gives 2.03, best 5 dates are only 2% of return, 74% of dates positive, positive mean in all 6 years. note: the earlier robustness checks were misleading for a structural reason worth remembering: dropping 2021 from a 2021-2026 sample only moves the window to 2022-2026, which was the good stretch. a robustness check inside a truncated sample cannot detect that the truncation IS the problem. the only fix was more data, not more checks.
verdict: REFUTED. the 1.66 was an artifact of a sample that began in 2021. 2018 (-0.44), 2019 (+0.95) and 2020 (-0.54) were flat to negative. on the full 8.8-year sample the strategy is 0.24 with t=0.69.

hypothesis: Everything tested so far asks 'which stock will outperform'. This asks a different question: WHEN does the equity premium accrue. Documented finding (Lachance 2023, Bogousslavsky JFE 2021, Berkman et al 2012) is that US equity returns accrue disproportionately overnight, with a mechanism: margin requirements are higher overnight and lending fees are charged on overnight positions, so arbitrageurs flatten before the close and mispricing persists to the open. Testable with the open and close data already loaded. Prediction: overnight return materially exceeds intraday; the open question is whether 252 round trips a year of cost leaves anything.
name: overnight vs intraday return decomposition

note: overnight premium is REAL: 62% of total return, 38% of variance, overnight sharpe 0.83 vs intraday 0.31 across 4.4m stock-days. NOT capturable: breakeven half-spread 2.01bp, large caps cost 2.1bp, so 252 round trips/yr nets -1.2%. only SPY at sub-1bp survives at 2-6%/yr vs 12% for holding it. the premium and the cost of harvesting it are the same size

conclusion: not a strategy. the 215th trial found a real feature of the data that cannot be converted into a position anyone can take.
distinction: a RISK PREMIUM is compensation for bearing a risk, and it is paid to whoever bears it. an EDGE is a mispricing, and it is paid to whoever identifies it. the overnight premium is the first kind. its breakeven half-spread is 2.01bp and large caps cost 2.1bp, so the market charges almost exactly what the premium pays to anyone trying to harvest it by trading. you collect it by HOLDING overnight, which is what every buy-and-hold investor already does.
issue: the registry reported this as CLEARING the bar with deflated p = 1.000. that is arithmetically right and substantively misleading, and the reason matters.
why: i passed n_obs = 3,210 daily observations. the luck bar scales with 1/sqrt(n), so a sample that large drops the bar to 0.35 and almost anything clears it. the overnight premium IS statistically real at that sample size. what it is not is an exploitable edge.

hypothesis: First test in this project driven by a MECHANISM rather than a pattern. When a stock joins the S&P 500, index funds tracking it are FORCED to buy on the effective date regardless of price. Documented by Shleifer 1986 and Harris & Gurel 1986: additions rise into the effective date on buying pressure, then partially reverse as the pressure ends. The forced buyer is the reason someone would pay me. Testing the post-effective reversal, which is what the effective date alone can measure. Known risk: recent literature finds the effect has decayed substantially as arbitrageurs front-run it. Sample is survivorship-biased toward additions that stayed in the index, and deletions are absent.
name: S&P 500 index addition effect

note: mechanism test. the run-up is SELECTION not forced buying: it stretches back a full year (-250 to -126 is +17.5%, t=7.14), because S&P adds companies that already grew. the forced-buying component is the post-effective reversal: shorting additions for 10 days nets +1.20% per event, t=2.18, 55% positive, 148 event dates over 12.7 years. sharpe 0.61 against a luck bar of 1.63, deflated p 0.041. consistent across periods (+0.44/+1.47/+1.80) and strengthening, not decaying. still fails the bar

hypothesis: The symmetric test to additions, and cleaner. Index funds must SELL a deleted name on the effective date. Deletions are not survivorship-biased the way additions are, since the sample is companies that kept trading after demotion rather than companies that stayed in the index. Acquisition-driven deletions are excluded by necessity (no post-event price) and arguably by correctness (price is pinned to deal terms, so there is no pressure reversal to measure). Prediction: a pre-event decline that is mostly SELECTION if it stretches back a year, plus a post-effective bounce if forced selling is real. Trade is to BUY deletions after the effective date.
name: S&P 500 deletion effect (forced selling)

note: deletions do NOT confirm additions. pre-event decline mirrors additions exactly (-15.9% from -250 to -126, t=-7.73) confirming selection. post-effective bounce is +0.59% t=0.67, not significant, against the addition reversal of -0.79% t=-2.09. combined long-deletions/short-additions book: 10d hold gives 0.82% per event, t=1.65, sharpe 0.46 vs a bar of 1.55, deflated p 0.025. the addition result does not survive its own symmetric test

hypothesis: Not a pattern and not a prediction: a contractual cash flow. Perpetual swaps have no expiry, so an 8-hourly funding payment tethers them to spot. When the perp trades above spot, longs pay shorts. Holding short perp against long spot is delta-neutral and collects that payment mechanically. The economic source is explicit: levered long demand in crypto persistently exceeds levered short demand, and the carry is the price of supplying that leverage. This is a RISK PREMIUM, not an edge, and it carries exchange counterparty risk that no backtest can capture. Testing whether the funding received survives trading costs, and whether it is large enough to matter after the crowding of recent years.
name: crypto perpetual funding carry

note: crypto perp funding carry. gross is real: median 10.5% annualized across 16 coins, 81% positive, 3.4 years, 71% of months positive. daily sharpe of 7.11 is an artifact (the measured variance is the wobble in a cash flow, not the risk of the trade). monthly sharpe 1.56 vs a luck bar of 3.07, deflated p 0.089. DECAYING HARD: 23.5% annualized in 2024, 6.3% in 2025, 1.7% in 2026. and the real risk is a tail nothing in the series captures: basis blowout, liquidation, venue failure

rule: Whatever the reproducible script produces replaces the README numbers for strategy 20, including if the carry gets larger. No keeping whichever version reads better.
statement: The published strategy 20 numbers have no analysis script in the repo, so nobody can reproduce them. Two defects are visible in the raw data before any analysis: (1) Hyperliquid settled every 8 hours until early June 2023 and hourly after, but annualization treats every print as hourly; (2) a large share of hourly prints sit at about 1.25e-5, which is Hyperliquid's fixed interest-rate component (0.01% per 8h, ~11% a year), not a market price of leverage. I am writing funding_carry.py to reproduce the result, fix the period-length bug, split funding into the fixed interest leg and the market premium leg, charge entry/exit costs, and use OKX daily perp and spot closes to measure the basis P&L the funding series leaves out. This revisits an existing hypothesis with corrected arithmetic and is not a new trial.

action: README numbers for strategy 20 replaced. Code and data moved to crypto/.
verdict: The published numbers came from truncated data. The Hyperliquid ingest returned [] after three failed requests and the pagination loop read that as end of history, cutting 9 of 16 coins off at exact multiples of 500 rows (AVAX after 44 days). The headline median barely moved (10.5% to 10.0%) but the story did: the median coin's market leg is -0.9% a year, so the entire median carry is Hyperliquid's fixed 11% interest constant, a parameter the venue sets, not a price of leverage. Against T-bills per dollar of capital it is 4.0% a year, monthly Sharpe 0.87 vs a bar of 3.07. All of that excess is 2024 (+12.3%); 2023, 2025 and 2026 are -1.0%, +1.4% and +0.5%. The published 2026 figure of 1.7% was a truncation artifact (true funding 6.0%), so the decay is not a collapse to zero, it is a collapse to the interest constant. Daily-close basis risk is small (worst coin-day -0.63%) but 30% three-day rallies, enough to liquidate an unrebalanced 3x short, occur 3.3 times per coin-year. Strategy 20 superseded by these numbers; trial count unchanged.

hypothesis: Strategy 20 showed the always-on carry beats T-bills by 4.0% a year per dollar of capital, all of it in 2024. Funding is strongly persistent because it reflects slow-moving levered-long demand, so trailing funding should forecast next-period funding. Rule: per coin, hold short perp / long spot only when trailing annualized funding, scaled by capital efficiency 1/(1+1/3), exceeds the current 3-month T-bill yield; otherwise hold T-bills. 32bp round trip charged on every switch on and off. Decision uses only data before the holding period. Variants: lookback 7 or 30 days x rebalance weekly or monthly. PRIMARY, named now: 30-day lookback, weekly rebalance. Prediction: the switch keeps most of 2024 and sits out 2023, 2025, 2026, so excess over T-bills rises and drawdown months shrink. The way it fails: funding turns over faster than a week, so switching costs eat the gain, or the switch is just late to every regime. Benchmarks: always-on carry (4.0% excess) and T-bills (0).
name: crypto funding carry, switched on trailing funding vs T-bills

note: switching the carry on trailing 30d funding vs T-bills (primary, weekly) lifts excess over T-bills from 4.0% to 5.9% a year per dollar of capital after switching costs, worst month -2.4% to -0.2%, 64% time on. all 4 variants 5.4-5.9%. no lookahead: peeking a week gives 6.5%, delaying 7/14/30 days decays smoothly 5.3/4.8/4.2. BUT the prediction was wrong about where it comes from: it does not sit out 2025-26 (excess 1.9%, 1.1%) because the 11% interest constant scaled by capital (8.25%) clears T-bills on its own, so the rule stays on while the negative market leg bleeds. the gain is 2023 (-1.0% to +8.9%), mostly avoiding SUI and AVAX through long negative-funding stretches with 5-7 coins in the book. a few episodes, not a regime signal. monthly sharpe 1.71 vs bar 3.08, deflated p 0.111
